routes.title: Add reproducible privacy tests to Brazil's AI inspection programme
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD), using its existing inspection programme.
routes.obligor: AI personal-data controllers selected for inspection; no specific controller has agreed to this pilot.
routes.instrument: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 30 of 23 December 2025, Mapa de Temas Prioritários 2026–2027, Annex Theme 4; existing inspection procedures described by ANPD.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: request a reproducible privacy/security test dossier in a selected AI inspection, including personal-data extraction tests, a model/version record and evidence that identified failures were corrected. Establish relevance and lawful evidence scope case by case.
routes.verification: Proposed Geneva pilot: preserve an initial failing test, remediation decision and blinded retest by 21–22 June 2027. Count inspected in-scope deployments with complete evidence against all in-scope deployments in the selected inspection cohort; publish aggregate results only.
routes.remedy: ANPD describes preventive correction and administrative sanction proceedings. A failed proposed benchmark would not itself establish a legal violation; connect any corrective action to an identified data-protection obligation.
routes.window: The adopted 2026–2027 map schedules 20 AI/emerging-technology inspection activities, half by the first half of 2027. That semester ends after the Geneva checkpoint; no individual inspection date or pilot allocation is confirmed.
routes.evidenceSummary: A named, adopted inspection programme provides a real implementation opportunity. It does not establish acceptance of the proposed test protocol or coverage of frontier-model risks beyond personal-data processing.
routes.gap: Inspection cohort, remaining 2026–2027 capacity, case-specific evidence authority and controller cooperation are unknown. Twenty activities are not twenty models, companies or deployments.
routes.nextQuestion: Which scheduled Theme 4 inspection can produce a lawful, reproducible remediation-and-retest record before 21 June 2027?
incentives: Proposed benefit: comparable technical evidence could help ANPD distinguish a paper response from corrected behaviour.
Proposed benefit: controllers obtain a bounded evidence request tied to an actual processing risk.
constraints: Personal-data jurisdiction does not confer a general model-release veto.
Inspection and sanction decisions remain with ANPD; regulated parties have procedural rights.
No matched deployment denominator or remaining-capacity figure was located.

routes.title: Attach AI test evidence to Mexico's public-sector privacy assessment
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno for the proposed federal-executive scope, together with a deploying public body to be selected.
routes.obligor: A public-sector personal-data controller undertaking a qualifying new or modified AI deployment.
routes.instrument: Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados (2025), arts.68–73: impact assessment and advance submission.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: append reproducible personal-data leakage and unauthorized-access tests to one qualifying assessment. Have the deploying body's own release decision record unresolved failures and retest criteria; obtain its agreement rather than treating the regulator's advice as binding.
routes.verification: Proposed: retain the dated assessment, submission receipt, recommendations, release decision and a retest by 21–22 June 2027. Measure deployments with complete tests over all qualifying deployments in the chosen body's defined pilot period; record exemptions separately.
routes.remedy: Assessment recommendations are expressly nonbinding. A proposed internal decision to pause deployment requires the public body's own authority and adoption; the assessment process is not a statutory AI approval veto.
routes.window: Standing trigger: submit 30 business days before qualifying deployment or modification. No actual late-2026/2027 AI deployment or open consultation was located; a pre-Geneva pilot is conditional on selecting one in time.
routes.evidenceSummary: Arts.68–73 supply a concrete procedure, defined timing and exemptions. The official-hosted consolidation identifies its latest amendment as 14 November 2025. A booked 2027 decision is not evidenced.
routes.gap: Need the selected deployment, current competent receiving unit, applicable assessment guidance and an exemption determination. Later amendments beyond the retrieved consolidation have not been exhaustively excluded.
routes.nextQuestion: Which federal-executive AI deployment has an arts.68–73 assessment due before May 2027, and will its deploying body adopt a documented test-and-retest release condition?
incentives: Proposed benefit: integrate evidence into an existing assessment instead of creating a new approval institution.
Proposed benefit: expose privacy failures before citizens' data enter a new system.
constraints: Nonbinding recommendations cannot be represented as mandatory model certification.
Article 73 exemptions may remove the assessment trigger.
Pilot and operational calendar remain unverified.

routes.title: Pilot AI risk evidence for Chile's high-risk data assessment duty
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Agencia de Protección de Datos Personales for assessment guidance, with a participating controller; operational readiness must be verified.
routes.obligor: A controller planning qualifying high-risk AI personal-data processing once the amended law applies.
routes.instrument: Ley 21.719 amendments to Ley 19.628, art.15 ter (impact assessments), and transitional commencement provisions; implementation timing is challenged by bill 18.623-07.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: incorporate a reproducible AI privacy-risk test and mitigation/retest annex in assessment guidance, then pilot it with one controller. Use a voluntary readiness exercise if legal commencement is deferred beyond Geneva.
routes.verification: Proposed Geneva evidence: approved pilot scope, completed risk assessment, seeded personal-data leak detected and repaired, and a retest showing whether the repair works. Distinguish voluntary readiness from legally required compliance.
routes.remedy: Article 15 ter noncompliance is listed in the law's infringement provisions, subject to commencement and procedure. The proposed testing annex has not been adopted; it is not an existing mandatory certification or model-release veto.
routes.window: Published law is scheduled for 1 December 2026. Senate reporting on 20 October 2026 describes proposed deferral to December 2027; its 28 October session record says the bill was approved in general and particular and sent to the Chamber of Deputies. Final passage/promulgation and the final replacement date are unverified. Do not promise enforceable implementation before 21–22 June 2027.
routes.evidenceSummary: Article 15 ter names high-risk assessments and agency guidance. The late-October deferral process is direct contrary evidence to a confident December-2026 implementation route.
routes.gap: Final bill status, operational agency appointments, issued guidance and a willing controller remain unverified. No open public consultation with a deadline was established.
routes.nextQuestion: What is the final status of bill 18.623-07, and can the agency or a controller complete a voluntary assessment-and-retest pilot before Geneva if commencement moves?
incentives: Proposed benefit: a readiness pilot can reveal implementation costs before guidance becomes binding.
Proposed benefit: controllers can test whether their mitigations address actual data leakage.
constraints: Deferral may put the enforcement window after Geneva.
Agency readiness cannot be inferred from statutory creation.
Support for delaying commencement is not support for this safeguard.

routes.title: Test remediation under Colombia's AI privacy-impact circular
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC), within its personal-data supervision jurisdiction.
routes.obligor: A supervised administrator of personal data developing or deploying an in-scope high-risk AI system; pilot entity unselected.
routes.instrument: SIC Circular Externa No.002 of 21 August 2024, instructions on personal-data processing in AI systems, especially high-risk impact studies and auditable security measures.
routes.safeguard: Proposed: turn one high-risk privacy-impact study into a testable evidence dossier, with model-versioned data-extraction tests, mitigation ownership and a documented retest. Seek a bounded pilot using the existing circular rather than assert a new general AI licensing power.
routes.verification: Proposed: retain initial risk finding, approved mitigation and repeatable retest before 21–22 June 2027. Measure the share of identified in-scope pilot systems with completed evidence, plus unresolved severe privacy failures.
routes.remedy: The circular calls for abstention or precautionary/preventive measures where uncertainty concerns serious irreversible harm from processing. Case-specific enforcement of legal duties requires the appropriate procedure; the new test threshold is not an existing automatic sanction trigger.
routes.window: Standing instrument can inform a late-2026/early-2027 supervised or voluntary pilot. No dated inspection, current consultation or selected deployment was verified. A purported annual work-programme lead could not be read and is not used as a decision window.
routes.evidenceSummary: The read circular specifically addresses AI, high-risk privacy studies and auditable security. It is stronger than an AI strategy as an instrument, but supplies no verified pre-Geneva pilot calendar.
routes.gap: Need a current SIC case or work-plan slot, named administrator, applicable procedural remedy and evidence-sharing agreement. Exact-scope leadership alignment is unknown.
routes.nextQuestion: Which current SIC-supervised high-risk AI project can expose an initial privacy failure and a verified repair before Geneva?
incentives: Proposed benefit: auditable tests make demonstrated accountability more concrete.
Proposed benefit: bounded remediation evidence can distinguish implementation from paperwork.
constraints: Personal-data safeguards cover a narrower risk class than catastrophic AI safety.
No confirmed 2027 operational slot or deployment denominator.
Do not treat a draft circular or an inaccessible work plan as an adopted new obligation.
